title: carex vulgaris subsp. dematranea
intro: Carex vulgaris subsp. dematranea, commonly known as  wood sedge, is a subspecies of perennial sedge native to Europe, Asia, and North Africa. It is used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, making it effective in treating various conditions such as wounds, digestive issues, and respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of wood sedge include anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifungal effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. These bioactive constituents work together to provide a range of health benefits, including reducing inflammation, fighting infections, and protecting against oxidative stress.
